items.title: LangGraph in production: Temporal's LangGraph Plugin adds Durable Execution
items.feed_description: LangGraph agents now run on Temporal: automatic crash recovery, free human-in-the-loop waits, and full observability via new LangSmith integration.
items.summary: Temporal announced a public preview release of its LangGraph plugin, enabling seamless integration of LangGraph agents with Temporal's durable execution platform. The integration allows LangGraph workflows to run without code changes, providing automatic failure recovery, long-running human-in-the-loop steps, and production-grade reliability. LangSmith integrations for Python and TypeScript are also now in public preview.
features: Durable execution of LangGraph workflows via Temporal Workflows and Activities
Automatic recovery from failures with checkpointed state resumption
Support for human-in-the-loop steps with durable waits (signals/timers)
Handling of long-running agents with continue-as-new and state persistence
Integration with LangGraph's Graph API and Functional API
LangSmith observability for trace context across distributed executions
items.why_it_matters: Developers can now deploy LangGraph agents in production with reliable recovery and scalability, eliminating manual orchestration while maintaining LangGraph's workflow definition capabilities.

items.title: July 15, 2026
items.feed_description: Try the new Astro experience This feature is in Preview . Astro's navigation now gives you a single view across your entire Organization instead of a single Workspace. Deployments, Dags, and Astro IDE projects all appear across Workspaces in one view, with Workspace context on every row. Filter to a specific Workspace when you need to, or work from the full picture across your Organization. Workspace, Organization, and personal settings now share a single settings layout. The homepage also surfaces: Recently Failed Dags : An Organization-wide table of failing Dags, sorted by failure rate, with time-range filters. Each row shows the Workspace and Deployment, run history, and two actions: Investigate with Otto and Open in Airflow . Jump Back In : A strip of recently visited Deployments, Dags, data products, and Astro IDE projects. Favorite Deployments : An Organization-wide view of Deployment health with All , Healthy , and Hibernating status filters. Each card shows status, cluster and repository context, and four metrics: Dag Runs, Tasks, Worker CPU, and Worker Memory. You can favorite Dags (Airflow 3.1+) and Deployments to pin them to the top of these views and filter to only your favorites. Enable the new experience from the banner in Astro. To switch back, go to Your Profile , click Edit next to Astronomer Labs , and turn off the Astro Next toggle. Switching between experiences doesn't change your pipelines or configuration.
items.summary: Astronomer released updates on July 15, 2026, including new features like Astro Next experience, Sub-Second Pipelines, and Otto integration. Key changes involve improved DAG management, deployment testing, and security enhancements. The release also introduces disaster recovery tools and environment object promotion.
features: Astro Next experience: Organization-wide views for Deployments, Dags, and IDE projects with Workspace filtering
Sub-Second Pipelines for Airflow 3.2+ deployments with event-driven scheduling and high-throughput support
Otto integration for pull request reviews, Dag failure investigation, and code suggestions
DAG-level access control with role-based permissions for deployments
Environment Manager migration tools for connections/variables
Disaster recovery configuration tab for clusters
IP access list protection against accidental self-lockout
items.why_it_matters: These updates improve collaboration, security, and performance for data teams managing Airflow workflows, with enhanced monitoring, faster pipeline execution, and better access control.

items.title: Why a context engine needs Durable Execution: How Unblocked rebuilt its ingestion backbone on Temporal
items.feed_description: See how Unblocked replaced bespoke ingestion orchestration with Temporal to run 1 million durable, observable AI context Workflows every day.
items.summary: Unblocked rebuilt its ingestion backbone using Temporal's Durable Execution to handle continuous, cross-source computation for its AI context engine. The migration replaced a custom actor model with Temporal's polyglot SDK and durable workflows, enabling resilience to failures and simplifying orchestration. The system now supports over 3.6 million active workflows across data sources, with code ingestion transitioning from Prefect.
features: Durable Execution for continuous state computation across heterogeneous sources
Polyglot SDK support (Kotlin, TypeScript, Python)
Deployment-free workflows with automatic checkpoint resumption
Observability via Temporal UI replacing custom admin tools
Integration with Asana, CI, Slack, and other data sources
items.why_it_matters: Temporal's durable workflows enable Unblocked to maintain accurate, real-time context for AI agents without caching, reducing operational complexity and improving reliability for developers and data teams.

items.title: Astro Observe data quality now in Preview
items.feed_description: This feature is in Preview . Astro Observe data quality for Snowflake and Databricks is now available in Preview. Data quality helps you monitor tables and columns for data quality issues including row volume changes, schema changes, and null columns, alerting on issues and displaying upstream and downstream table-level lineage to help keep your data accurate and complete. See data quality for setup and more information. Additional improvements Astro Observe SLAs now support flexible cron-based schedules to capture complex business logic and allow more control over SLA sensitivity.
